questions.question: Which famous Shabbat piyyut did Dunash ben Labrat compose?
questions.explanation: "Dror Yikra" is sung at Shabbat tables in all the communities of Israel, in many melodies, from Yemen to Georgia. It expresses longing for redemption within the rest of Shabbat.

questions.question: In which city was Dunash born and educated?
questions.explanation: Dunash was born in Fez, Morocco, around 920. The city was then a vibrant spiritual and cultural center.

questions.question: Under whom did Dunash study in Babylonia?
questions.explanation: Dunash studied in Babylonia in the yeshiva of Rav Saadia Gaon, and there he was exposed to the methods of analysis of Arabic and Hebrew and began to compose poems.

questions.question: Who invited Dunash to Cordoba?
questions.explanation: Hasdai ibn Shaprut, the minister and leader of the Jews of Cordoba, sought to establish in Spain an independent center of Torah, poetry and science, and gathered the finest minds to himself.

questions.question: True or false: Dunash was the first to introduce into Hebrew poetry the quantitative meter of Arabic poetry.
questions.explanation: Until his time, Hebrew poetry and piyyut had not been composed according to the rules of quantitative meter. The meter he introduced became the hallmark of Hebrew secular poetry in Spain.

questions.question: What is the name of the system of meter that Dunash introduced into Hebrew poetry?
options: The meter of yatedot (pegs) and tenuot (movements)
questions.explanation: Hebrew does not distinguish between short and long vowels as Arabic does, and so Dunash built the meter from "yatedot" (pegs) and "tenuot" (movements). Poets used this system for generations.

questions.question: With whom did Dunash conduct the great grammatical controversy in Cordoba?
questions.explanation: The debate between Dunash and Menachem ben Saruq was also a cultural and theological struggle, which stirred the Jews of Spain and continued through their students.

questions.question: Which linguistic principle did Dunash champion, and Menachem ben Saruq opposed?
options: Interpreting Scripture according to Kabbalah only
Comparing Hebrew with Arabic in order to understand difficult words in Scripture
Giving up the vocalization of Scripture
questions.explanation: Dunash argued that the two languages share a common Semitic origin, and therefore the rules of Arabic shed light on Hebrew. Menachem regarded Hebrew as a unique divine language that must not be compared.

questions.question: True or false: In the acrostic of "Dror Yikra" the name of Hasdai ibn Shaprut, Dunash's patron, is signed.
questions.explanation: In the initial letters of the first, second, third and sixth stanzas the name "Dunash" is signed, and this is evidence that he is the author of the piyyut.

questions.question: Which work of Menachem ben Saruq did Dunash criticize in his "Teshuvot" (Replies)?
options: A commentary on the Babylonian Talmud
The "Mahberet," a dictionary of the words of Scripture
A prayer book for the communities of Spain
questions.explanation: "Mahberet Menachem" is a comprehensive dictionary of biblical words. In it Menachem identified many roots as consisting of only one or two letters.

questions.question: True or false: In the Cairo Genizah, poems were found that Dunash and his wife, who was herself a poet, exchanged.
questions.explanation: Mournful poems that Dunash and his wife wrote when he was forced to wander were found in the Genizah, and they attest that she was an important poet in her own right.

questions.question: True or false: Menachem's students enthusiastically accepted the new meter that Dunash introduced.
questions.explanation: Menachem's students sharply attacked the meter and claimed that Dunash was corrupting biblical Hebrew, because in order to meet the meter he altered biblical forms.

questions.question: True or false: Dunash also disagreed with his teacher, Rav Saadia Gaon, and wrote critiques of his commentaries on Scripture.
questions.explanation: Dunash composed about two hundred grammatical and exegetical critiques of the translations and commentaries of Rasag, in the work "The Replies of Dunash ben Labrat on Rasag."

questions.question: Which other work of Dunash, in the same meter, is accepted to this day in the Ashkenazi communities?
options: "Devai Haser," the opening of the invitation to the Seven Blessings meal
questions.explanation: "Devai Haser" was written in the same meter as "Dror Yikra," and both works became part of the liturgy of Shabbat and of joy.

questions.question: Which sage composed "Safah Yeterah" in defense of Rav Saadia Gaon against Dunash's critiques?
questions.explanation: Ibn Ezra regarded Rasag as a supreme authority, and composed "Safah Yeterah" in the city of Lucca in Italy in 1140–1142.

questions.question: Which exegete, active in France in the eleventh century, cites Dunash's words in his commentary on Scripture?
questions.explanation: Dunash's influence is evident in Rashi's commentary on Scripture, which cites his words as an anchor for understanding the plain meaning of words.

questions.question: True or false: Rabbenu Tam, Rashi's grandson, ruled in most cases in favor of Dunash against Menachem.
questions.explanation: In the "Sefer HaHakhra'ot" Rabbenu Tam analyzed the claims of both sides, and in most cases ruled in favor of Menachem ben Saruq.

questions.question: Why did Rabbenu Tam rule in most cases in favor of Menachem?
options: Because of a family relationship between him and Menachem
Because of his conservative outlook, which preferred the tradition of the text over innovations and reconstructions
Because Dunash's critiques were written in Arabic and were not understood in France
Because Hasdai ibn Shaprut asked this of him
questions.explanation: Rabbenu Tam came out against those who alter versions of texts on the basis of their own reasoning, and even criticized his brother, the Rashbam. For the same reason he preferred Menachem's conservative grammar.

questions.question: Which grammarian, a student of Menachem, ultimately adopted the principle of comparison with Arabic and established that the Hebrew root is built of three consonants?
questions.explanation: It was precisely the student of his great rival who adopted the principle for which Dunash fought, and with its help he established Hebrew grammar on three fixed consonants.

questions.question: What is a "yated" (peg) in the meter that Dunash introduced?
options: A closed syllable at the end of a line
A rhyme that repeats at the end of each stanza
A mobile shva or a hataf, followed by a full vowel
questions.explanation: Dunash equated the mobile shva and the hataf vowels with the short vowels in Arabic. A "yated" is a mobile shva or a hataf followed by a vowel, and a "tenuah" is an ordinary syllable.
